title: How Precious Is the Book Divine
description: How Precious Is the Book Divine in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 189 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Value of the Scriptures”, where the book credits them to Rippon's Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: How pre-cious is the book di-vine, By in-spi-ra-tion given! Bright as a lamp its doc-trines shine, To lead our souls to heaven.

lines: How precious is the book divine,
Bright as a lamp its doctrines shine,
To lead our souls to heaven.
O'er all the strait and narrow way
A light whose never weary ray
It sweetly cheers our fainting hearts
In this dark vale of tears;
Life, light, and comfort it imparts,
This lamp through all the dreary night
Of life shall guide our way,
Till we behold the glorious light
